# Interactive Legend Cross-Filter Sales Dashboard (Vega-Altair)

## Background

You are building an offline, self-contained analytics dashboard with the declarative visualization library https://altair-viz.github.io/ (Altair 5+). A retail analyst wants a single dashboard where clicking an entry in the color legend focuses the whole dashboard on one product category, dimming the others in a summary view and hiding the others in a trend view. The dashboard must work entirely offline (no network access) once opened in a browser.

The input dataset is already present on disk as a local CSV file. You must NOT download any remote dataset or reference any external URL.

## Requirements

* Load the local sales data and build ONE combined Altair chart composed of two vertically stacked linked views that share a single interactive legend:
  * A **stacked bar view**: total monthly sales, with bars stacked and colored by product category.
  * A **time-series line view**: monthly sales over time drawn as one line per product category.
* Add a single clickable point selection over the `category` field, bound to the color legend, and shared by both views (so one legend controls the entire dashboard).
* In the stacked bar view, use a conditional encoding so the selected category is fully opaque while the non-selected categories are dimmed.
* In the time-series line view, use a transform filter driven by the same selection so that only the selected category's line is shown (when nothing is selected, all lines are shown).
* Save the result as a single self-contained HTML file that renders without any network access.

## Implementation Hints

* Use Altair 5+ syntax. An interactive legend is created by binding a point selection to the legend, and a single selection object can be reused across concatenated views.
* Conditional opacity can be expressed with Altair's when/then/otherwise (or condition) helper; the trend view can be narrowed with a filter transform that references the same selection.
* Compose the two views into one chart (vertical concatenation) so a single HTML file contains both.
* The bar view should aggregate sales to a monthly sum per category; the line view should show the monthly sales value per category over time.
* Project path: /home/user/project
* Input data file: /home/user/project/data/sales.csv (columns: `date` (ISO date string, first day of each month), `category` (product category name), `sales` (integer units sold)).
* Output file: /home/user/project/dashboard.html
* Ensure the generating script is actually executed so that the output HTML artifact exists on disk.
* The saved HTML must be self-contained and render offline: it must embed the Vega/Vega-Lite/vega-embed runtime and the full data inline (do NOT emit a spec that points at the CSV path or any http(s) data URL).
* The embedded Vega-Lite spec must contain: a point selection parameter with `bind` set to `legend` and projected on the `category` field; a bar mark with a stacked quantitative encoding and a conditional opacity encoding; and a line mark whose view carries a filter transform referencing the selection.

The resulting HTML embeds the full Vega/Vega-Lite/vega-embed JS and all data inline so it renders without any network access. """ import json import pathlib import csv # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 1. Load the CSV data into a plain list-of-dicts (no pandas dependency) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- DATA_PATH = pathlib.Path("/home/user/project/data/sales.csv") OUTPUT_PATH = pathlib.Path("/home/user/project/dashboard.html") records = [] with DATA_PATH.open(newline="") as fh: reader = csv.DictReader(fh) for row in reader: records.append({ "date": row["date"], # "YYYY-MM-DD" "category": row["category"], "sales": int(row["sales"]), }) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 2. Build the Vega-Lite spec by hand so we have full, explicit control over # every feature required: legend-bound point selection, conditional opacity, # and a filter transform referencing the selection. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Shared colour scale – four categories, pleasant palette COLOR_SCALE = { "domain": ["Clothing", "Electronics", "Furniture", "Groceries"], "range": ["#e07b39", "#4c78a8", "#72b7b2", "#54a24b"], } # ---- Selection parameter (shared across both views via top-level params) -- # bind: "legend" → clicking a legend entry fires the selection SELECTION_PARAM = { "name": "cat_select", "select": { "type": "point", "fields": ["category"], }, "bind": "legend", } # ---- Stacked bar view ------------------------------------------------------- bar_view = { "mark": {"type": "bar"}, "encoding": { "x": { "field": "date", "type": "temporal", "timeUnit": "yearmonth", "title": "Month", "axis": {"format": "%b %Y", "labelAngle": -45}, }, "y": { "field": "sales", "type": "quantitative", "aggregate": "sum", "title": "Total Sales", "stack": "zero", }, "color": { "field": "category", "type": "nominal", "scale": COLOR_SCALE, "title": "Category", # Legend must be present so the bind:"legend" target exists "legend": {"title": "Category — click to filter"}, }, # Conditional opacity: selected → fully opaque; others → dimmed. # When nothing is selected (empty selection) every bar is fully opaque. "opacity": { "condition": { "param": "cat_select", "value": 1.0, }, "value": 0.15, }, "tooltip": [ {"field": "category", "type": "nominal", "title": "Category"}, {"field": "date", "type": "temporal", "timeUnit": "yearmonth", "title": "Month", "format": "%b %Y"}, {"field": "sales", "type": "quantitative", "aggregate": "sum", "title": "Total Sales"}, ], }, "title": "Monthly Sales by Category (Stacked)", "width": 700, "height": 300, } # ---- Time-series line view -------------------------------------------------- # transform: filter by the selection so only the selected category is shown. # An empty selection matches everything → all lines visible when none selected. line_view = { "transform": [ {"filter": {"param": "cat_select"}}, ], "mark": {"type": "line", "point": True, "strokeWidth": 2.5}, "encoding": { "x": { "field": "date", "type": "temporal", "timeUnit": "yearmonth", "title": "Month", "axis": {"format": "%b %Y", "labelAngle": -45}, }, "y": { "field": "sales", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Sales", }, "color": { "field": "category", "type": "nominal", "scale": COLOR_SCALE, "title": "Category", "legend": None, # legend lives only on the bar view }, "tooltip": [ {"field": "category", "type": "nominal", "title": "Category"}, {"field": "date", "type": "temporal", "timeUnit": "yearmonth", "title": "Month", "format": "%b %Y"}, {"field": "sales", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Sales"}, ], }, "title": "Monthly Sales Trend (click legend above to filter)", "width": 700, "height": 250, } # ---- Top-level combined spec ------------------------------------------------ spec = { "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json", "title": { "text": "Retail Sales Dashboard", "subtitle": "Click a legend entry to focus; click again to clear", "fontSize": 20, "subtitleFontSize": 13, "anchor": "start", }, # Inline data – no external CSV reference "data": {"values": records}, # Shared parameter declared at the top level so BOTH views see it "params": [SELECTION_PARAM], "vconcat": [bar_view, line_view], "resolve": {"scale": {"color": "shared"}}, "config": { "background": "#fafafa", "view": {"stroke": "transparent"}, "font": "system-ui, sans-serif", }, } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 3. Produce the self-contained HTML # We embed the three Vega JS libraries as inline
""" return html # Try altair-based save first; fall back to manual build try: import altair as alt # noqa: F401 html_content = build_html_altair(spec) method = "altair" except Exception as exc_altair: print(f"[INFO] altair save failed ({exc_altair}); building HTML manually …") try: html_content = build_html_manual(spec) method = "manual (inline CDN bundles)" except Exception as exc_manual: raise RuntimeError( f"Both HTML-build strategies failed.\n altair: {exc_altair}\n manual: {exc_manual}" ) from exc_manual OUTPUT_PATH.write_text(html_content, encoding="utf-8") print(f"[OK] Dashboard written to {OUTPUT_PATH} (method: {method})") print(f" File size: {OUTPUT_PATH.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB")

"""
Build a self-contained, offline-capable Altair 6 dashboard.

Views:
  1. Stacked bar chart  – total monthly sales per category
                          legend-bound point selection + conditional opacity
  2. Time-series lines  – monthly sales per category
                          filter transform driven by the same selection

The two views share one `selection_point` parameter bound to the colour legend.
Saved with `inline=True` so all Vega/Vega-Lite/vega-embed JS is embedded and
the file renders with zero network access.
"""

import csv
import pathlib
import altair as alt

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the CSV data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA_PATH   = pathlib.Path("/home/user/project/data/sales.csv")
OUTPUT_PATH = pathlib.Path("/home/user/project/dashboard.html")

records: list[dict] = []
with DATA_PATH.open(newline="") as fh:
    for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
        records.append({
            "date":     row["date"],        # "YYYY-MM-DD"  (ISO, first of month)
            "category": row["category"],
            "sales":    int(row["sales"]),
        })

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Shared colour scale and selection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COLOR_SCALE = alt.Scale(
    domain=["Clothing", "Electronics", "Furniture", "Groceries"],
    range= ["#e07b39", "#4c78a8", "#72b7b2", "#54a24b"],
)

# Point selection projected on "category" and bound to the colour legend.
# When nothing is selected the selection is empty (empty=True default) which
# means the condition evaluates to True for every row → all bars fully opaque,
# all lines visible.
cat_select = alt.selection_point(
    name="cat_select",
    fields=["category"],
    bind="legend",
)

# Shared x encoding (month)
x_enc = alt.X(
    "yearmonth(date):T",
    title="Month",
    axis=alt.Axis(format="%b %Y", labelAngle=-45),
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Stacked bar chart
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
bar = (
    alt.Chart(alt.InlineData(values=records))  # inline → no CSV path in spec
    .mark_bar()
    .encode(
        x=x_enc,
        y=alt.Y(
            "sum(sales):Q",
            title="Total Sales",
            stack="zero",
        ),
        color=alt.Color(
            "category:N",
            scale=COLOR_SCALE,
            title="Category",
            legend=alt.Legend(title="Category — click to filter"),
        ),
        # Conditional opacity: selected category → 1.0 ; others → 0.15
        opacity=alt.condition(cat_select, alt.value(1.0), alt.value(0.15)),
        tooltip=[
            alt.Tooltip("category:N",        title="Category"),
            alt.Tooltip("yearmonth(date):T",  title="Month",       format="%b %Y"),
            alt.Tooltip("sum(sales):Q",       title="Total Sales"),
        ],
    )
    .properties(
        title="Monthly Sales by Category (Stacked)",
        width=720,
        height=310,
    )
    # Attach the selection to this view (it drives the legend here)
    .add_params(cat_select)
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Time-series line chart
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
line = (
    alt.Chart(alt.InlineData(values=records))
    .transform_filter(cat_select)          # only the selected category is drawn
    .mark_line(point=True, strokeWidth=2.5)
    .encode(
        x=x_enc,
        y=alt.Y("sales:Q", title="Sales"),
        color=alt.Color(
            "category:N",
            scale=COLOR_SCALE,
            legend=None,            # legend lives only on the bar view
        ),
        tooltip=[
            alt.Tooltip("category:N",       title="Category"),
            alt.Tooltip("yearmonth(date):T", title="Month",  format="%b %Y"),
            alt.Tooltip("sales:Q",           title="Sales"),
        ],
    )
    .properties(
        title="Monthly Sales Trend  (click legend above to focus a category)",
        width=720,
        height=260,
    )
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compose and save
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
dashboard = (
    alt.vconcat(bar, line)
    .resolve_scale(color="shared")
    .properties(
        title=alt.TitleParams(
            text="Retail Sales Dashboard",
            subtitle="Click a legend entry to focus · click again to clear",
            fontSize=22,
            subtitleFontSize=13,
            anchor="start",
        )
    )
    .configure_view(stroke="transparent")
    .configure(background="#fafafa", font="system-ui, sans-serif")
)

# inline=True  →  Vega / Vega-Lite / vega-embed JS are embedded in the file
dashboard.save(
    OUTPUT_PATH,
    format="html",
    inline=True,
    embed_options={"renderer": "canvas", "actions": True},
)

size_kb = OUTPUT_PATH.stat().st_size / 1024
print(f"[OK] Saved: {OUTPUT_PATH}  ({size_kb:,.0f} KB, fully self-contained)")

import pathlib, json, re

html = pathlib.Path("/home/user/project/dashboard.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

# Extract the embedded Vega-Lite spec JSON from the HTML
match = re.search(r'var spec\s*=\s*(\{.*?\});\s*var embedOpt', html, re.DOTALL)
if not match:
    # Try alternate pattern used by altair 6
    match = re.search(r'"spec"\s*:\s*(\{.*?\})\s*\};\s*vegaEmbed', html, re.DOTALL)
if not match:
    # Dump whatever is between 'var spec =' and the next semicolon
    match = re.search(r'var spec\s*=\s*(\{.+)', html, re.DOTALL)

raw = match.group(1)
# Trim to first balanced brace block
depth, end = 0, 0
for i, ch in enumerate(raw):
    if ch == '{': depth += 1
    elif ch == '}':
        depth -= 1
        if depth == 0:
            end = i + 1
            break
spec = json.loads(raw[:end])
print("Schema:", spec.get("$schema", "(none)"))

# ---- Check: selection param with bind=legend ----
params = spec.get("params", [])
vconcat = spec.get("vconcat", [])

# Flatten params from all layers
all_params = list(params)
for layer in vconcat:
    all_params += layer.get("params", [])
    for sub in layer.get("layer", []):
        all_params += sub.get("params", [])

legend_sel = [p for p in all_params
              if isinstance(p.get("bind"), str) and p["bind"] == "legend"
              or isinstance(p.get("bind"), dict) and p["bind"].get("input") == "legend"]
print("legend-bound selection params:", [p.get("name") for p in legend_sel])

# ---- Check: bar mark with stacked encoding and conditional opacity ----
def find_marks(node, marks=None):
    if marks is None: marks = []
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        m = node.get("mark") or {}
        mark_type = m if isinstance(m, str) else m.get("type", "")
        if mark_type:
            marks.append((mark_type, node.get("encoding", {})))
        for v in node.values():
            find_marks(v, marks)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            find_marks(item, marks)
    return marks

all_marks = find_marks(spec)
bar_marks  = [(t, enc) for t, enc in all_marks if t == "bar"]
line_marks = [(t, enc) for t, enc in all_marks if t == "line"]

print(f"\nBar marks found : {len(bar_marks)}")
for _, enc in bar_marks:
    y = enc.get("y", {})
    stack = y.get("stack") if isinstance(y, dict) else None
    opacity = enc.get("opacity", {})
    has_condition = "condition" in opacity if isinstance(opacity, dict) else False
    print(f"  y.stack={stack}, opacity has condition={has_condition}")

print(f"\nLine marks found: {len(line_marks)}")

# ---- Check: filter transform referencing the selection ----
def find_filter_transforms(node, hits=None):
    if hits is None: hits = []
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        transforms = node.get("transform", [])
        for t in transforms:
            if "filter" in t:
                filt = t["filter"]
                if isinstance(filt, dict) and "param" in filt:
                    hits.append(filt["param"])
        for v in node.values():
            find_filter_transforms(v, hits)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            find_filter_transforms(item, hits)
    return hits

filter_params = find_filter_transforms(spec)
print(f"\nFilter transforms referencing params: {filter_params}")

# ---- Check: data is inline (no CSV path or http URL) ----
spec_str = json.dumps(spec)
has_csv_ref  = "sales.csv" in spec_str
has_http_url = "http://" in spec_str or "https://" in spec_str
print(f"\nData is inline (no CSV path): {not has_csv_ref}")
print(f"Data is inline (no http URL in spec): {not has_http_url}")
print(f"Sales records in spec: {'2023-01-01' in spec_str}")

# ---- Check: JS is embedded (not CDN link) ----
has_cdn_script = 'src="https://' in html or "src='https://" in html
has_inline_vega = "vegaEmbed" in html and "<script>" in html
print(f"\nNo external <script src=https://...> tags: {not has_cdn_script}")
print(f"vega-embed code inlined: {has_inline_vega}")

print("\nALL CHECKS PASSED" if (
    legend_sel and bar_marks and line_marks and filter_params
    and not has_csv_ref and not has_http_url and not has_cdn_script
    and has_inline_vega
) else "\n*** SOME CHECKS FAILED ***")
EOF
